name: Morphine

binding.notes: Chen 1991. In the Volpe 2011 uniform-assay ranking of recombinant human MOR (PMC, doi:10.1016/j.yrtph.2010.12.007) morphine fell in the Ki=1-100 nM bin.

binding.tissue_or_cell: CHO membranes expressing recombinant human MOR
binding.notes: Volpe et al. 2011 — morphine classified in Ki = 1–100 nM bin; uniform-assay re-ranking. Volpe 2011 is a uniform radioligand BINDING panel and reports no functional efficacy; an Emax previously attached to this row has been removed rather than left attributed to a study that did not measure it.
binding.assay_notes: uniform radioligand binding, [3H]-DAMGO, 19-drug single-assay panel
[35S]GTPγS, operational tau
binding.notes: derived as tau_morphine/tau_DAMGO = 5.2/28.5 from retrieved tau values 5.2 ± 0.2 and 28.5 ± 1.1. Table 1 EC50/Emax columns not reliably extractable; operational KA reported in the same table as 97.5 ± 28.5 nM but from an extraction pass that scrambled adjacent columns, so recorded null.

binding.tissue_or_cell: human µ receptor (WT), recombinant in AtT20
binding.assay_notes: GIRK / membrane potential with β-CNA receptor depletion, operational tau
binding.notes: printed directly in Table 1 as 0.18 ± 0.02 (abstract and Table 2 print 0.17 ± 0.02). Operational pKA 6.38 ± 0.3. Absolute operational tau in this system 15.4 ± 4 (DAMGO 90 ± 22).

binding.assay_notes: TRUPATH BRET Gαi1 dissociation
binding.notes: The same paper measures morphine at 71-72% of DAMGO in an unamplified nanobody conformational sensor and 31-32% in βarr2 assays — a clean illustration that morphine's apparent 'full agonism' is receptor reserve, not intrinsic efficacy (cf. relative tau 0.18).

binding.tissue_or_cell: mixed (heterologous cell lines and endogenous tissue)
binding.assay_notes: meta-summary across [35S]GTPγS, Ca2+ channel inhibition and K+ current assays
binding.notes: cross-study mean ± SEM of 0.19 ± 0.08 for the operational-analysis subset; mean across ALL analysis methods 0.36 ± 0.07, individual study range 0.02-0.72. Included as a sanity band, not as an axis value. It says the honest thing: morphine's published relative efficacy spans 0.02-0.72 depending on assay and analysis, and operational analysis lands near 0.19 — which is where both source-A and source-B independently land.

binding.assay_notes: [35S]GTPγS on human mu-CHO membranes (Emax, EC50); Ki by [3H]DAMGO displacement, human mu-CHO
binding.notes: The only set in this file with Ki and Emax from one lab, one receptor preparation, one species. DAMGO's own EC50 in this system is 13.7 ± 5.28 nM and its Ki is 0.5 ± 0.05 nM.

functional.notes: Morphine recruits β-arrestin-2 with intermediate efficacy compared with DAMGO; this is the comparator against which 'G-protein biased' opioids (TRV130, mitragynines) are normalised.

biased_agonism.interpretation: Morphine is the canonical reference compound used to define β-arrestin-2 over-recruitment liability; some analyses place it as marginally arrestin-biased relative to DAMGO, but the 'biased agonism rescues respiratory depression' hypothesis (originating from Bohn 1999/2000, KO mice) is now contested.

receptor_oligomerisation.functional_consequence: Morphine binding at μ in μ/δ heteromer shifts pharmacology; δ-antagonists potentiate morphine analgesia and slow tolerance.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Gαi/o coupling → inhibition of adenylyl cyclase (decreased cAMP), activation of GIRK potassium channels (hyperpolarisation), inhibition of N/P/Q-type Cav channels (decreased neurotransmitter release). Repeated activation drives GRK-mediated phosphorylation, β-arrestin-2 recruitment, receptor desensitisation and internalisation (morphine internalises MOR poorly compared with DAMGO/etorphine — the 'RAVE' paradox).

routes.notes: F% ranges 20-40% due to high first-pass UGT2B7 glucuronidation; oral AUC ratios M3G:morphine ≈ 30:1, M6G:morphine ≈ 5:1.

metabolism.notes: M3G has been implicated in opioid-induced hyperalgesia/neuroexcitation (TLR4) but is not an MOR agonist.
M6G accumulates in renal failure → prolonged sedation/respiratory depression. Penetrates BBB poorly but acts at MOR with higher intrinsic potency than parent.

drug_interactions_pk.mechanism: rifampicin induction of morphine clearance/transport (P-gp); the source explicitly found NO evidence of UGT induction
drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: morphine AUC reduced ~28% and Cmax ~41%; complete loss of analgesic effect in the crossover study

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: OPRM1 118G carriers show ~2x lower brain MOR binding potential, need ~30% more morphine for the same analgesia, but are paradoxically protected against morphine-induced respiratory depression (OR 5.6 for AA vs G-carriers). UGT2B7*2 alters M6G/M3G ratio. COMT Val158Met affects pain processing and morphine requirement.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Receptor internalisation by morphine is paradoxically weaker than DAMGO; tolerance is driven more by signalling adaptation than receptor loss. Functional desensitisation occurs over days.
cross_tolerance: all MOR full agonists (heroin, oxycodone, hydromorphone, fentanyl)
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Onset 6-12 h after last dose; peak 36-72 h; lasts 5-10 days. Symptoms: rhinorrhoea, lacrimation, mydriasis, piloerection, myalgia, abdominal cramps, diarrhoea, autonomic hyperactivity, dysphoria.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Proposed mechanism for opioid-induced hyperalgesia; clinical importance debated.

demographic_differences.sex: Women report stronger analgesia from morphine at equivalent plasma concentrations; mechanism likely receptor sensitivity rather than PK.
demographic_differences.age: Elderly (>65) have ~50% reduced clearance and higher Cmax; reduce dose 25-50%.
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Renal failure: M6G/M3G accumulate dramatically → reduce dose, lengthen interval, or switch to hydromorphone/fentanyl.

data_gaps_remaining: definitive human cloned MOR Ki measured in same lab as comparators
notes: Morphine is the reference opioid; all relative potencies in clinical use are anchored to it.

name: 6-Monoacetylmorphine

binding.notes: Selley et al. 2001 — 6-MAM has affinity near-equal to morphine but greater efficacy than morphine in stimulating [35S]GTPγS binding at MOR. Higher Emax explains heroin > morphine rush at equimolar exposure.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Same Gαi cascade as morphine; greater intrinsic efficacy at MOR; also activates DOR (Negus et al. 1994, pmid:8138935).

routes.notes: 6-MAM is the dominant heroin metabolite in blood for the first 30 min; crosses BBB more efficiently than heroin or morphine but is restricted by P-gp/BCRP.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: P-gp ablation in mice doubles brain accumulation of 6-MAM and morphine.

data_gaps_remaining: human cloned MOR Ki measured against DAMGO
notes: 6-MAM, not morphine, drives the acute rush after intravenous heroin (Gottås 2019, pmid:31268284).

name: Heroin

binding.notes: Heroin itself binds MOR with low intrinsic affinity; pharmacology is dominated by rapid hydrolysis to 6-MAM and morphine.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Acts predominantly as a lipophilic prodrug; rapid esterase hydrolysis (t½ ≈ 2-3 min) to 6-MAM then morphine. The fast onset/'rush' reflects BBB penetration of the diester rather than direct receptor activity.

routes.notes: Parent heroin half-life ~2-6 min; undetectable by 10-40 min. Effects driven by 6-MAM then morphine.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: Same OPRM1 sensitivity as morphine; CES1 polymorphism could in principle alter hydrolysis but is not clinically established.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: As morphine but more abrupt — onset 4-8 h, peak 36-72 h, duration 5-10 d.

demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Renal failure prolongs M6G accumulation — same caveat as morphine.

notes: Heroin is functionally a lipophilic morphine pro-prodrug. Naloxone reverses heroin overdose by antagonising MOR occupied by 6-MAM/morphine.

name: Buprenorphine

binding.tissue_or_cell: CHO membranes expressing recombinant human MOR
binding.notes: Sub-nanomolar MOR Ki; very slow off-rate explains long clinical duration and difficulty in displacement during overdose.
Functional KOR antagonism contributes to mood-elevating effects and is the basis for buprenorphine's antidepressant signal.
Weak NOP partial agonism — proposed to modulate reward and may contribute to reduced abuse liability.

binding.assay_notes: [35S]GTPγS, operational tau
binding.notes: derived as 0.6/28.5 from retrieved tau values 0.6 ± 0.1 and 28.5 ± 1.1. Lowest intrinsic efficacy of the classical clinical opioids — ~1/9 of morphine. Reproduced at 0.02 on human MOR in source-B.

binding.tissue_or_cell: human µ receptor (WT), recombinant in AtT20
binding.assay_notes: GIRK / membrane potential with β-CNA receptor depletion, operational tau
binding.notes: printed as 0.02 ± 0.008. Operational pKA 7.42 ± 0.4; absolute tau 1.9 ± 0.3.

binding.assay_notes: TRUPATH BRET Gαi1 dissociation
binding.notes: Same paper: buprenorphine Emax 81% at Gαz and 65-66% at GαoA/oB, i.e. its partial agonism is Gα-subtype dependent; 24% of DAMGO in the unamplified nanobody sensor.

binding.assay_notes: [35S]GTPγS on human mu-CHO membranes; Ki by [3H]DAMGO displacement
binding.notes: The only sub-maximal agonist in Toll's mu panel — but the ±36 error bar is more than half the value, so treat 66% as 'clearly partial, magnitude uncertain'. Toll's own commentary is that GTPγS binding cleanly identifies partial agonists such as buprenorphine. Toll's Ki of 1.5 ± 0.8 nM is ~7x looser than Volpe's 0.2157 nM — the largest disagreement between the two uniform human panels.

binding.tissue_or_cell: human MOR (full-length OPRM1) in Chem-5 cell membranes
binding.assay_notes: uniform radioligand binding, [3H]-DAMGO
binding.notes: Second-highest affinity of the 19 (only sufentanil is tighter), while carrying the lowest intrinsic efficacy of the clinical panel (relative tau ~0.02). Highest affinity + lowest efficacy is the blockade/ceiling profile in one line. source-T disagrees at 1.5 ± 0.8 nM.

functional.notes: Virk & Williams 2009 / J. Neurosci. — buprenorphine Emax ~25-40% of full agonists; intrinsic efficacy at MOR is low.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Partial Gαi activation, very slow MOR dissociation (>2 h), poor internalisation. Norbuprenorphine metabolite is a FULL agonist at MOR, DOR, NOP — and 10× more respiratory-depressant than parent in rats (Brown 2011, doi:10.1016/j.taap.2011.02.014) — BUT does not cross the human BBB efficiently, which is why buprenorphine's clinical respiratory ceiling holds. Buprenorphine itself competitively blocks norbuprenorphine from CNS MOR (Brown 2011).

neuroimaging.finding: 16 mg sublingual buprenorphine produces ~80-95% MOR occupancy that persists 24-76 h; this is the basis for once-daily and depot dosing.

routes.notes: Oral F% <10% due to first-pass; sublingual ≈30%. Effective elimination half-life 24-42 h.

concentration_effect.notes: Dahan 2006 — respiratory depression plateaus at ≈50% of baseline minute ventilation, the famous ceiling effect.

metabolism.notes: Picard 2005 — CYP3A4 dominant, CYP2C8 minor contributor. Norbup is a full MOR/DOR/NOP agonist but has poor BBB penetration in humans.
Brown 2011 — both glucuronides are biologically active at opioid receptors.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP3A4 polymorphisms and inducers/inhibitors meaningfully alter buprenorphine and norbuprenorphine AUC. OPRM1 118G carriers may need higher maintenance doses.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Very slow MOR off-rate (>2 h dissociation) means antagonist effects persist; withdrawal symptoms milder and slower-onset than full agonists.
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Onset 24-72 h after last dose; peak 5-7 d; milder but more protracted than morphine; insomnia and dysphoria last weeks.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Clinically meaningful QT prolongation rare; no torsades signal in routine use.

demographic_differences.age: Elderly: reduce initial dose; longer half-life.
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Hepatic impairment: large F% changes; avoid in severe liver disease. Renal failure: no major dose change needed.

notes: The respiratory ceiling effect — partial agonism at MOR limits maximal respiratory depression — is the safety feature that makes bup viable for opioid use disorder maintenance. Naloxone reversal of buprenorphine overdose requires HIGH doses (≥2-4 mg) and may not fully overcome the slow off-rate.

name: Methadone

binding.notes: R-methadone is the active opioid enantiomer; ~10× higher MOR affinity than S.
Bossert 2023 — S-methadone is a MOR partial agonist with selectively reduced efficacy at MOR-Gal1R heteromer; low abuse liability.
Non-competitive NMDA antagonist; both enantiomers equipotent. Believed to contribute to efficacy in opioid-tolerant patients and neuropathic pain.
Eap 2007 — (S)-methadone blocks hERG 3.5× more potently than (R).

binding.assay_notes: [35S]GTPγS, operational tau
binding.notes: derived as 18.2/28.5 from retrieved tau values 18.2 ± 0.9 and 28.5 ± 1.1. Highest intrinsic efficacy of the clinical opioids in this set — ~3.5x morphine. Value independently corroborated in the Kelly 2013 review text (10.1111/bph.12222).

binding.assay_notes: [35S]GTPγS on human mu-CHO membranes; Ki by [3H]DAMGO displacement. Compound tested was (-)-methadone (the active R-enantiomer)
binding.notes: Exceeds DAMGO. This is the human-receptor corroboration of source-A's finding that methadone has the highest intrinsic efficacy of the clinical panel (relative tau 0.64). Note the enantiomer: (-)-methadone, not the racemate that is dispensed.

binding.tissue_or_cell: human MOR (full-length OPRM1) in Chem-5 cell membranes
binding.assay_notes: uniform radioligand binding, [3H]-DAMGO
binding.notes: Volpe tested the racemate as dispensed; source-T tested (-)-methadone and got 0.6 ± 0.2 nM. The ~5.6x gap is at least partly the enantiomer.

receptor_oligomerisation.functional_consequence: S-methadone has selectively low efficacy at this complex, which is implicated in opioid reward; this is offered as a mechanism for low abuse liability of (S)-MTD (REL-1017/esmethadone).

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: MOR Gαi cascade + non-competitive NMDA antagonism + SERT/NET reuptake inhibition. The NMDA antagonism is hypothesised to reduce opioid tolerance and treat neuropathic pain.

routes.notes: Eap 2002 — half-life highly variable (8-59 h), median ~24 h. F% high but inter-individual variability is enormous.

concentration_effect.notes: Daily methadone dose >100 mg / serum >1000 ng/mL associated with increased TdP risk.

metabolism.notes: CPIC 2024 guideline — CYP2B6 dominant; CYP3A4/5 contributes <5% by recent modelling. CYP2D6 minimal.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Precipitates methadone withdrawal in maintenance patients

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2B6 *6/*6 (slow metabolisers) have ~50% higher S-methadone plasma concentrations → 4.5× increased TdP risk (Eap 2007). CPIC 2024 recommends genotype-informed dosing.

cross_tolerance: all MOR full agonists (partial — NMDA antagonism modifies cross-tolerance)
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Onset 36-72 h, peak 6-10 d, lasts 3-6 weeks; protracted dysphoria common.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: QT prolongation, TdP, sudden cardiac death. ECG before initiation and at steady state recommended; risk ↑ above 100 mg/d.
Binds σ1; clinical relevance unclear.
Weak serotonin reuptake inhibition; documented serotonin toxicity reactions, including fatalities, when combined with MAOIs (including linezolid and moclobemide).

demographic_differences.age: Elderly: slower clearance, prolonged half-life — start low, go slow.
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Modest changes with renal impairment; faecal excretion compensates. Hepatic impairment: caution.

notes: Methadone half-life >> analgesic duration (4-8 h) means accumulation is the killer — overdose deaths cluster in week 1 of initiation. Rotating from morphine equivalents requires the conservative methadone-specific conversion (not linear with morphine).

name: Codeine

binding.notes: Codeine MOR Ki ~200× weaker than morphine; analgesia depends almost entirely on CYP2D6 O-demethylation to morphine (~10% of dose).

binding.assay_notes: uniform radioligand binding (source-E, [3H]DAMGO / Chem-5 hMOR); no functional efficacy source retrieved
binding.confidence: HIGH for affinity, LOW for efficacy
binding.notes: STILL A HOLLOW MARKER FOR EFFICACY, but affinity is now measured. Volpe 2011 Table 2: Ki 734.2 nM — the second-weakest binder of the 19-drug human panel. Toll 1998 Table 5 independently gives 135.2 ± 10.7 nM at human mu-CHO ([3H]DAMGO), i.e. the two uniform human panels disagree by ~5.4x on codeine while agreeing to within 6% on morphine; the weak-binder conclusion is robust, the point value is not. Codeine is absent from Toll's Table 7, so no human Emax exists in either panel. Efficacy class is well documented clinically (low-potency prodrug, analgesia largely via CYP2D6 O-demethylation to morphine). Peckham & Traynor 2006 (10.1124/jpet.105.094276) measured codeine's [35S]GTPγS efficacy side by side with morphine — still inaccessible.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Codeine itself is a weak MOR agonist; activity derives from CYP2D6 → morphine. Codeine-6-glucuronide (UGT2B7) is a minor active metabolite.

metabolism.notes: Rate-limiting bioactivation step; PMs get ~96% lower morphine AUC, UMs get supratherapeutic morphine from normal codeine doses.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Phenoconverts EM to PM → loss of codeine analgesia

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2D6 UM (≥3 functional copies, ~1-2% Caucasian, 30% Ethiopian): risk of fatal morphine intoxication from standard doses — multiple infant deaths reported in breastfeeding UM mothers and post-tonsillectomy children → FDA contraindicated codeine <12 yo (2017). CYP2D6 PM (~5-10% Caucasian): no analgesia. CPIC strongly recommends genotype-guided dosing or alternative.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Mild morphine-type withdrawal at chronic doses.

demographic_differences.age: AVOID in children <12 y and adolescents <18 y post-tonsillectomy (FDA black box).
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Renal failure: morphine and M6G accumulate; reduce dose.

notes: Codeine is the textbook CYP2D6 pharmacogenetics example — PMs get no analgesia, UMs get respiratory depression. NEJMa041888 reports the seminal infant death case.

name: Tramadol

binding.notes: Raffa 1992 — parent tramadol Ki ≈ 2.1 μM (weak); analgesia largely from M1 (O-DSMT).
(+)-tramadol enantiomer dominates SERT inhibition.
(−)-tramadol enantiomer dominates NET inhibition.

binding.assay_notes: uniform radioligand binding, single-assay panel of 19 approved opioids
binding.notes: Ki 12.486 µM is printed in the retrieved abstract as the weakest binder of the 19-drug panel — the quantitative statement that tramadol itself is essentially a prodrug at MOR. Use the O-desmethyltramadol row (source-B) for the efficacy axis.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Two parallel mechanisms: (1) parent tramadol + M1 → MOR Gαi cascade; (2) parent → SERT/NET inhibition → enhanced descending inhibition. M1 (O-desmethyltramadol) is the dominant opioid effector.

metabolism.notes: M1 has ≈200× higher MOR affinity than parent; clinical analgesia largely depends on M1.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2D6 PMs: poor analgesia (low M1). UMs: respiratory depression from low doses, multiple paediatric deaths; FDA contraindicates tramadol in children <12 y. CPIC 2021 guideline.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Hybrid opioid + serotonergic/noradrenergic discontinuation syndrome — opioid (sweating, GI) PLUS atypical (panic, paraesthesias, hallucinations, severe insomnia) lasting 5-15 d.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Lowers seizure threshold; risk amplified by SSRIs, bupropion, TCAs, and at supratherapeutic doses.
Minor 5-HT3 antagonism may contribute to anti-emetic / analgesic profile.

demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Reduce dose in CKD and cirrhosis.

notes: The serotonergic and seizure liability separates tramadol from classical opioids and creates DDI risks (SSRIs, MAOIs, linezolid) that don't apply to morphine.

name: O-desmethyltramadol

binding.notes: Raffa 1992 — (+) enantiomer is the potent MOR agonist; ≈400× more potent than parent (+)-tramadol.

binding.tissue_or_cell: human µ receptor (WT), recombinant in AtT20
binding.assay_notes: GIRK / membrane potential with β-CNA receptor depletion, operational tau
binding.notes: printed as 0.08 ± 0.02. This is the CYP2D6-derived active metabolite, not tramadol itself. Tramadol parent has no intrinsic-efficacy number in this file; its uniform-assay human MOR Ki is 12.486 µM (source-E), i.e. the parent is a prodrug at MOR. Operational pKA 5.33 ± 0.4.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: MOR Gαi cascade; retains tramadol-like monoamine effects but with much greater opioid contribution.

routes.notes: As metabolite of tramadol or when administered directly (desmetramadol clinical trials NCT04683926).

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: Bypasses CYP2D6 phenoconversion when administered directly; OPRM1 sensitivity applies as for any MOR agonist.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Inherits tramadol's seizure liability via mono­amine reuptake inhibition.

data_gaps_remaining: direct human Cmax for orally administered O-DSMT alone
notes: O-DSMT is the true opioid in tramadol therapy. When sold as a research chemical it bypasses CYP2D6 phenoconversion, making dosing more predictable but eliminating tramadol's 'self-limiting' poor-metaboliser safety margin.

name: Oxycodone

binding.notes: Volpe 2011 uniform assay; ~15× weaker than morphine at hMOR but oral F% and BBB transport compensate.
binding.assay_notes: uniform radioligand binding, [3H]-DAMGO
[35S]GTPγS, operational tau
binding.notes: derived as 5.1/28.5 from retrieved tau values 5.1 ± 0.2 and 28.5 ± 1.1. Essentially identical to morphine in this system; reproduced independently in source-B on human MOR.

binding.tissue_or_cell: human µ receptor (WT), recombinant in AtT20
binding.assay_notes: GIRK / membrane potential with β-CNA receptor depletion, operational tau
binding.notes: Table 1 prints 0.16 ± 0.03; Table 2 prints 0.16 ± 0.02. Operational pKA 5.39 ± 0.3; absolute tau 13.9 ± 2.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: MOR Gαi cascade; some active influx transport into rat brain (parental oxycodone, not metabolites, dominates CNS effect in humans).

metabolism.notes: Lalovic 2006 — major pathway; noroxycodone has negligible MOR activity.
Oxymorphone has 40-60× higher MOR affinity than oxycodone but contributes only ≈15% of analgesia in EMs because plasma exposure is low.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Reduces oxymorphone formation; small reduction in subjective effects

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2D6 status modulates oxymorphone formation but oxycodone's parent activity means PM/UM effect is smaller than for codeine/tramadol. CYP3A inhibition is the bigger clinical lever.

demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Hepatic impairment: 2× AUC, halve dose. Renal failure: parent accumulates.

notes: Unlike codeine/hydrocodone, oxycodone has meaningful intrinsic MOR activity, so CYP2D6 status is less critical clinically.

name: Hydromorphone

binding.notes: Volpe 2011 — sub-nanomolar, in Ki<1 nM tier with oxymorphone/buprenorphine. ~5× morphine potency in clinical use.
binding.assay_notes: uniform radioligand binding (source-E, [3H]DAMGO / Chem-5 hMOR); no functional efficacy source retrieved
binding.confidence: HIGH for affinity, LOW for efficacy

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: MOR Gαi; no significant active metabolites in normal renal function.

metabolism.notes: H3G has been associated with neuroexcitation/myoclonus in renal failure; analogous to morphine-3-glucuronide.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: UGT2B7*2 (-840G>A) modestly alters PK in some Asian populations.

demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Renal failure: H3G accumulates → myoclonus, seizures.

notes: Often preferred over morphine in renal failure because H3G is less neurotoxic than M3G, though debated.

name: Hydrocodone

primary_targets: MOR (mostly via hydromorphone metabolite in EMs; some direct activity)

binding.notes: Volpe 2011 — Ki ~40 nM. Hydromorphone has 10-100× higher affinity, so CYP2D6 conversion meaningfully contributes.
binding.assay_notes: uniform radioligand binding (source-E, [3H]DAMGO / Chem-5 hMOR); no functional efficacy source retrieved
binding.confidence: HIGH for affinity, LOW for efficacy

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Hybrid of direct MOR activation + CYP2D6→hydromorphone bioactivation.

metabolism.notes: Km 26 μM high-affinity CYP2D6 step; PMs have ~50% reduced subjective effects.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: ↓ hydromorphone exposure; some reduction in analgesia

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2D6 PMs have reduced analgesia; UMs may have exaggerated effects but less dramatic than codeine because parent has intrinsic activity.

notes: Functionally between codeine and oxycodone — parent has meaningful MOR activity, but CYP2D6 still matters.

name: Oxymorphone

binding.notes: Volpe 2011 — sub-nanomolar, one of the highest-affinity classical opioids. 40-60× more potent than oxycodone at MOR.
binding.assay_notes: uniform radioligand binding (source-E, [3H]DAMGO / Chem-5 hMOR); no functional efficacy source retrieved
binding.confidence: HIGH for affinity, LOW for efficacy

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: MOR Gαi.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: Less CYP-dependent than oxycodone; few clinically significant pharmacogenetic interactions.

demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Hepatic impairment dramatically increases oral F%; avoid in moderate-severe cirrhosis.

notes: Bypasses CYP-mediated metabolism; useful in patients on enzyme inhibitors.

name: Mitragynine

binding.notes: Várfi/Kruegel 2016, JACS — Ki ~233 nM (also reported 161-700 nM across labs). Partial agonist, low intrinsic efficacy (Emax ~30-50% of DAMGO).
binding.assay_notes: BRET G protein (Gα-RLuc8/Gγ-mVenus) dissociation

functional.notes: Kruegel/Majumdar 2016 — essentially no β-arrestin-2 recruitment → strongly G-protein biased.

biased_agonism.interpretation: Mitragynine is G-protein biased (recruits β-arrestin-2 essentially not at all), which is the proposed mechanism for kratom's apparently lower respiratory depression at equianalgesic doses vs morphine. The 'biased agonism = safer opioid' hypothesis is now controversial (Conibear & Kelly 2019 / doi:10.1016/j.tips.2019.04.002) — much of the safety may come from low intrinsic efficacy / partial agonism, not bias per se.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: MOR partial Gαi without β-arrestin-2; some α2-adrenergic and weak 5-HT2 activity contribute to subjective profile. CYP3A4 converts mitragynine to 7-hydroxymitragynine in vivo — 7-OH-MG is the dominant pharmacologically active species after oral kratom (Kruegel 2019).

routes.notes: Trakulsrichai 2015 — Tmax 0.83 h, t½ 23 h (range 9-43 h, dose-dependent). Cmax dose-dependent.
Huestis 2024 — t½ 42.9 h after high single dose, 61 h after multiple dosing.

metabolism.notes: Kruegel 2019 — CYP3A4 generates 7-OH-MG in vivo; 7-OH-MG is the dominant analgesic species after oral kratom.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Tanna 2024 — itraconazole ↑ mitragynine AUC ~3× and reduces 7-OH-MG (less bioactivation).
Mitragynine is a potent competitive CYP2D6 inhibitor in human liver microsomes (IC50 2.2 uM, Ki 1.1 uM); may cause clinically significant interactions with CYP2D6 substrates.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP3A inhibition reduces 7-OH-MG formation and may reduce kratom's opioid effects; OPRM1 sensitivity applies to the MOR component.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Mild-moderate opioid withdrawal — rhinorrhoea, myalgia, anxiety, restlessness, insomnia; usually milder and shorter than full agonists but well-documented (10-15% of chronic users meet DSM criteria).

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Some in vitro hERG block at supratherapeutic concentrations; rare QT signal in case reports.

data_gaps_remaining: definitive biased-agonism quantification in matched-lab conditions
notes: Mitragynine is a partial MOR agonist with G-protein bias, but in vivo most of kratom's opioid effect after oral dosing comes from CYP3A4-derived 7-hydroxymitragynine, which is a near-full MOR agonist (Kruegel 2019).

name: 7-Hydroxymitragynine

binding.notes: Kruegel/Majumdar 2016 — ~5× higher MOR affinity than mitragynine. Other recent measurements report 47-78 nM.
binding.assay_notes: BRET G protein (Gα-RLuc8/Gγ-mVenus) dissociation

functional.notes: Poor β-arrestin-2 recruitment — G-protein biased; the bias is the cited safety hypothesis.

biased_agonism.interpretation: Strongly G-protein biased; in mice, 7-OH-MG produces analgesia with reduced respiratory depression and constipation vs morphine at equianalgesic doses (Chakraborty 2019/2021). However, abuse liability is real — case reports of physical dependence and overdose are accumulating as concentrated 7-OH products proliferate on the market.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Near-full Gαi cascade at MOR with minimal β-arrestin-2 recruitment.

routes.notes: Huestis 2024 — 7-OH-MG t½ ~2.5 h after kratom tea; minor exposure compared with parent mitragynine. Direct 7-OH-MG dosing produces much higher Cmax and longer half-life.

metabolism.notes: Majumdar 2016 — pseudoindoxyl rearrangement product is also a G-protein-biased MOR agonist.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Opioid-type withdrawal; concentrated 7-OH products produce rapid tolerance and dependence resembling full agonists.

notes: 7-OH-MG is the dominant in-vivo opioid effector after oral kratom (Kruegel 2019, ACS Cent Sci). Concentrated 7-OH-MG products (tablets, gummies) marketed as 'kratom alternatives' since 2023 deliver receptor agonism in the same potency tier as morphine and carry corresponding overdose risk. The G-protein bias does not eliminate abuse liability.

name: Kratom

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Multi-alkaloid mixture; major constituents are mitragynine (60-66% of alkaloid mass), paynantheine (8-9%), speciogynine (6-7%), 7-hydroxymitragynine (≤2%), speciociliatine, mitraphylline. Pharmacology is dominated by mitragynine and its CYP3A4-derived 7-OH-MG metabolite (Kruegel 2019).

routes.notes: Trakulsrichai 2015 — mitragynine PK in 10 chronic kratom users (Thailand). Mitragynine Cmax ~105 ng/mL after typical brewed-tea dose.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Mild to moderate opioid withdrawal in regular users; well-characterised but generally less severe than morphine/heroin withdrawal.

notes: Crude kratom leaf is dramatically safer than concentrated 7-OH-MG extracts because in raw kratom 7-OH-MG comprises ≤2% of alkaloid mass.

name: Tapentadol

binding.notes: Tzschentke 2007 — Ki 96 nM at cloned hMOR (some sources quote 60 nM at rat MOR). ~50× weaker than morphine yet only 2-3× less analgesic in vivo due to NRI synergy.
Tapentadol has only weak SERT activity (>30× selectivity for NET vs SERT) → much lower serotonin-syndrome risk than tramadol.

binding.tissue_or_cell: human µ receptor (WT), recombinant in AtT20
binding.assay_notes: GIRK / membrane potential with β-CNA receptor depletion, operational tau
binding.notes: printed as 0.05 ± 0.01. First published quantification of tapentadol intrinsic efficacy. Operational pKA 5.4 ± 0.3 (low-micromolar functional affinity). Clinically its analgesia is part noradrenaline-reuptake inhibition, so mu efficacy alone understates the drug; the paper cites an estimated 'µ-load' of ~40%. At 30 µM tapentadol directly interferes with the GIRK signal — an off-target artifact, above therapeutic plasma levels (~100-560 nM).

functional.notes: Manandhar 2022 — tapentadol has lower intrinsic efficacy at MOR than morphine or oxycodone (partial agonist character at MOR).

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: MOR Gαi + central noradrenergic inhibition → synergistic analgesia. NET-mediated descending pain modulation contributes most of analgesia at typical doses.

metabolism.notes: Glucuronidation dominates clearance — NOT CYP-dependent; minimal DDI footprint and minimal pharmacogenetic CYP impact.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Hypertensive crisis with MAOIs (contraindicated). Serotonin syndrome risk lower than tramadol because SERT activity minimal.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: Unlike tramadol/codeine, tapentadol does NOT depend on CYP2D6 bioactivation — no PM/UM dichotomy. UGT2B7 polymorphisms produce modest exposure differences.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Mixed opioid + adrenergic discontinuation; generally milder than morphine.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Less seizure risk than tramadol; lacks SERT activity.

demographic_differences.age: Elderly: small reduction in clearance, no dose adjustment usually needed.
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Hepatic: avoid in severe impairment (>3× AUC). Renal: avoid in severe CKD.

notes: Mechanistically cleaner than tramadol: NRI dominates, SERT minimal, no CYP2D6 bioactivation. Safer pharmacogenetic and DDI profile.

name: Pentazocine

binding.notes: (-)-pentazocine is the KOR analgesic; provides analgesia + dysphoria.
(+)-pentazocine is the canonical σ1 radioligand.
Weak partial MOR agonist; can precipitate withdrawal in MOR-tolerant patients.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: KOR Gαi (analgesia + dysphoria/dysphoric hallucinations); σ1 modulation (psychotomimesis); MOR partial agonism.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Atypical — opioid + dysphoria; can precipitate acute withdrawal in MOR-dependent patients.

data_gaps_remaining: quantitative Ki values from a single paper
notes: Classic mixed agonist-antagonist; will precipitate withdrawal in MOR-tolerant patients.

name: Butorphanol

binding.notes: Gharagozlou 2003 — high-affinity KOR partial agonist.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: KOR-dominant analgesia + MOR partial agonism. Ceiling for respiratory depression.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Mixed opioid/dysphoric; less severe than morphine.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Weak σ binding (Ki > 1 μM); minimal contribution to clinical effects.

notes: Like pentazocine but with stronger KOR affinity and weaker σ component → less dysphoria.

name: Demerol

binding.notes: Volpe 2011 — ~10% morphine potency at MOR; clinical analgesia equivalent to ~10 mg morphine per 75-100 mg meperidine.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: MOR Gαi; weak SERT block (serotonin syndrome with MAOIs is classic); normeperidine has CNS-stimulant/proconvulsant activity (non-opioid, possibly NMDA-related).

metabolism.enzyme: CYP2B6 / CYP3A4 / CYP2C19 (N-demethylation; 57/28/15% of intrinsic clearance)
metabolism.notes: Normeperidine has half the analgesia but several-fold the proconvulsant activity; t½ ~15-30 h; accumulates with repeat dosing → seizures.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Severe serotonin syndrome, hyperpyrexia, death — ABSOLUTE contraindication.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2B6 slow metabolisers accumulate parent, less normeperidine, fewer seizures.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Mild anticholinergic effects.
Local anaesthetic activity (relevant to spinal/epidural use).
Repeated dosing → normeperidine accumulation → tremor, myoclonus, generalised seizures — naloxone does NOT reverse.

demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Renal failure: normeperidine accumulates dramatically — avoid.

notes: Largely replaced in modern practice because of normeperidine toxicity. Multiple guidelines list it as 'avoid except brief use'.

primary_targets: MOR (parent has direct activity unlike codeine)

binding.notes: Schmidt 2003 — dihydrocodeine Ki 14 μM; CYP2D6→dihydromorphine has 60× higher affinity.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Hybrid of direct (low) MOR activation + CYP2D6→dihydromorphine bioactivation.

metabolism.notes: Fromm 1995 — CYP2D6 O-demethylation; PMs have impaired dihydromorphine formation. Unlike codeine, parent dihydrocodeine retains some analgesia in PMs.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: ↓ dihydromorphine formation; some loss of analgesia (less dramatic than codeine).

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2D6 polymorphism alters dihydromorphine exposure but parent compound contributes meaningfully to analgesia.

name: Desomorphine

binding.notes: Casati 2017 review. Desomorphine is a full MOR agonist; in animal models 8-10× morphine potency due to high lipophilicity → rapid BBB entry.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: MOR Gαi.

routes.notes: Fast onset (15-30 s IV), short duration (1-2 h).

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Severe and rapid morphine-type withdrawal owing to short half-life.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Devastating necrotising soft-tissue lesions in krokodil users are caused by reactive impurities (phosphorus, iodine, hydrochloric acid) from clandestine codeine→desomorphine synthesis — NOT desomorphine itself.

notes: Pure desomorphine is a clean potent MOR agonist; krokodil's notoriety reflects toxic synthesis impurities.

name: Dextropropoxyphene

binding.notes: Weak MOR agonist (Chen 1991); analgesic potency similar to codeine.
Ulens 1999 — both propoxyphene and norpropoxyphene block hERG; low-dose facilitates, high-dose blocks.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Weak MOR Gαi + dose-related cardiac Na+ and K+ channel block driving the proarrhythmia that led to worldwide withdrawal (2009-2010).

routes.notes: Norpropoxyphene t½ 30-36 h — long enough to accumulate to cardiotoxic concentrations.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Norpropoxyphene blocks cardiac Na+ channels more potently than lidocaine, quinidine, procainamide → QRS widening, arrhythmias.
QT prolongation, TdP. Drug withdrawn from US (2010), EU (2009), UK (2005) primarily for this reason.

notes: Withdrawn worldwide due to dose-related cardiotoxicity from norpropoxyphene accumulation.

name: Propoxyphene

binding.notes: Generic 'propoxyphene' = racemate; analgesia resides in the dextro-isomer.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Same as dextropropoxyphene.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Same cardiotoxicity profile as dextropropoxyphene — withdrawn from market.

notes: See Dextropropoxyphene entry — same compound, racemic form.

name: Tilidine

binding.notes: Schulz 2004 — parent tilidine has weak MOR affinity; nortilidine is the selective MOR agonist that crosses BBB.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Prodrug → nortilidine (active) → bisnortilidine (inactive). Naloxone co-formulation prevents IV abuse (oral naloxone has near-zero F% but blocks parenteral activity).

routes.notes: Extensive first-pass to nortilidine; combination with naloxone (Valoron N) reduces IV abuse.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2C19/2B6 polymorphisms alter nortilidine exposure.

notes: Used widely in Germany/Switzerland; abuse-deterrent naloxone formulation.

name: Levomethorphan

binding.notes: Levorphanol Ki ~1.4 nM at hMOR; similar profile across MOR/DOR/KOR + NMDA + SNRI.
Non-competitive NMDA antagonist, contributes to neuropathic analgesia.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Demethylated to levorphanol by hepatic CYP enzymes; levorphanol provides the actual pharmacology (MOR full agonism + NMDA antagonism + SNRI activity).

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Morphine-type, delayed onset due to long half-life.

notes: Levomethorphan is the levo-enantiomer of racemethorphan (DXM is the dextro-enantiomer with no opioid activity). Prodrug to levorphanol.

name: Ethylmorphine

binding.notes: Like codeine, parent ethylmorphine has low MOR affinity; activity from CYP2D6→morphine conversion.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: CYP2D6 O-deethylation to morphine; CYP3A4 N-demethylation to norethylmorphine. Same pharmacogenetics as codeine.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: Same PM/UM caveats as codeine.

notes: Largely historical; used in some European countries as cough/antitussive.

name: Nicomorphine

binding.notes: Prodrug — rapidly hydrolysed to 6-mononicotinoyl-morphine, then morphine. 2-3× more potent than morphine in vivo.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Esterase hydrolysis to nicotinic acid + morphine; analogous to heroin's diester strategy for faster BBB entry.

routes.notes: Rectal F% of morphine and metabolites after nicomorphine ~88%.

notes: Used in Austria/Germany for cancer pain.

name: Opium

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Crude raw opium contains morphine 10-12% by weight (dominant analgesic alkaloid), codeine 0.5-3%, thebaine 0.5-2%, plus the smooth-muscle alkaloids papaverine and noscapine. CNS pharmacology dominated by morphine.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: Same as morphine + codeine.

notes: Crude plant material; effects dominated by morphine content. Variable alkaloid content per source.

name: Pst

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Aqueous extract of poppy seeds (Papaver somniferum) — pharmacology is morphine + codeine + thebaine eluted from seed-coat residue. Highly variable: morphine 1-2788 mg/kg of seed, codeine <1-248 mg/kg, thebaine <1-124 mg/kg (Powers 2018).

routes.notes: Pharmacokinetics dominated by morphine; same first-pass UGT2B7.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: Same as morphine + codeine.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Morphine-type; can be severe with chronic use because daily morphine dose from PST can reach 100-500 mg.

notes: The dose hazard is extreme variability — a single washed-seed batch can be inert; the next can deliver lethal morphine.

name: Apomorphine

binding.notes: Highest-affinity target.
Range 35-103 nM across studies.
Despite morphine-derived name, apomorphine has NO meaningful opioid receptor activity. Naloxone does not reverse its emetic/dyskinetic effects.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Broad D1/D2-like dopamine agonism; potent area-postrema D2 stimulation causes profuse vomiting (the classic emetic effect).

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Apomorphine can prolong QT; avoid in patients with QT-prolonging meds.

notes: Despite morphinan name, apomorphine is a dopamine agonist with NO opioid activity — categorisation under 'classical opioids' is historical/structural, not pharmacological.

name: 3-HO-PCP

binding.notes: 8× more potent than PCP at NMDA; high-affinity uncompetitive antagonist.
Ki 39-60 nM; unusually high MOR affinity for an arylcyclohexylamine (PCP itself: Ki 11-26 μM).

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Dual MOR agonist + NMDA antagonist + σ1 binding — the combination of opioid analgesia and NMDA-mediated dissociation makes 3-HO-PCP qualitatively different from other PCP analogues.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Opioid + dissociative withdrawal possible with chronic use.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: MOR agonism means overdoses produce opioid-type respiratory depression — UNLIKE pure NMDA antagonists like ketamine. Naloxone-reversible respiratory depression has been reported in fatalities.

notes: Unique among PCP analogues: high-affinity MOR agonism on top of NMDA antagonism means naloxone IS appropriate for overdose, unlike PCP/3-MeO-PCP overdose where naloxone is irrelevant.

name: U-51754

binding.notes: Vasudevan 2022 — U-51754 was the most potent KOR agonist in a panel of U-series compounds (EC50 120 nM); shows that pyrrolidine substitution shifts selectivity toward KOR. Unlike U-47700, NOT a μ-selective agonist.
Much weaker than U-47700 at MOR.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: KOR-selective; expect dysphoria/psychotomimesis rather than euphoria; respiratory effects different from MOR opioids.

notes: Often miscategorised as 'methylene-U47700' — actually structurally distinct (pyrrolidine vs dimethylamine) → KOR-selective profile. Naloxone has lower affinity at KOR than MOR; reversal of KOR overdose less predictable.

name: W-15

binding.notes: Huang 2017 — no detectable opioid receptor activity for W-15 or W-18 up to 10 μM. The 'designer opioid' marketing of W-15/W-18 was based on a pharmacology error; in fact they are NOT opioids.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: No opioid action. Detected in fatalities only in polydrug context. Likely off-target targets unknown.

notes: W-15 and W-18 were widely sold as 'designer opioids' but Huang et al. 2017 (PMC5752382) showed both lack any detectable activity at MOR/DOR/KOR/NOP. Naloxone is therefore irrelevant for overdose.

name: Bromadol

binding.notes: In vivo potency originally reported as 10,000× morphine; modern hot-plate work gives ~500× morphine, 2.9× fentanyl. trans-isomer >> cis. Direct Ki at recombinant hMOR not published.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: MOR full agonist; ultra-high potency means microgram doses are active and unintentional overdose risk extreme.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Microgram-active → extreme overdose risk; naloxone reversible but may require multiple doses.

notes: Cyclohexanol scaffold (not morphinan, not fentanyl). Trans-isomer is the active form. Microgram potency means extreme overdose risk.

name: Dipipanone

binding.notes: Dipyanone (pyrrolidino analogue) EC50 ~40 nM, Emax 155% of hydromorphone — likely similar for dipipanone (piperidino analogue). Methadone-class.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Methadone-class MOR full agonist; ~2.5× more potent than morphine in clinical use.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Methadone-class compounds carry baseline QT risk; specific dipipanone hERG data sparse.

notes: Sold combined with cyclizine (Diconal) — known for high abuse potential.

name: Palfium

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: MOR Gαi; high oral F% (almost as effective PO as IV).

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Morphine-type; rapid onset because short half-life.

notes: Short duration (1-3 h) + high oral F% drove high abuse potential — withdrawn from many markets.

name: Ketobemidone

binding.notes: Kristensen 1996 — high-affinity MOR full agonist; analgesic potency similar to morphine.
Weak NMDA block (Ki 26 μM); proposed to confer neuropathic-pain efficacy.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: MOR Gαi + weak non-competitive NMDA antagonism; spinal application blocks wind-up more effectively than morphine.

notes: Like methadone, the NMDA antagonism is proposed to be useful for neuropathic pain. Used in Scandinavia.

name: Acetorphine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Bentley-series oripavine derivative; semi-synthetic from thebaine via Diels-Alder. Non-selective μ/δ/κ agonist; analgesic potency several thousand times morphine. Acetylation of the 3-phenol increases lipophilicity vs etorphine.

notes: Schedule I; veterinary M99 reversed with diprenorphine. Microgram-active — extreme overdose risk.

name: Acetyldihydrocodeine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Acetate ester prodrug of dihydrocodeine; CYP2D6 O-demethylation produces dihydromorphine. Higher lipophilicity than dihydrocodeine should give faster onset.

notes: Minor opium-adjacent semi-synthetic; little dedicated pharmacology.

name: 6-mddm

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Hydromorphone derivative with 6-methylidene replacement; ~80× morphine MOR potency in animal hot-plate (Boswell 1968). Similar respiratory depression to morphine but less GI inhibition.

notes: Never developed clinically; included for completeness.

name: Ic-26

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Methadone analogue with carbonyl replaced by sulfone (bioisostere). Roughly methadone-equipotent in animals; human reports inconsistent.

notes: Sulfone bioisostere of methadone.

name: Isomethadone

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Methadone isomer with methyl group on different carbon; MOR full agonist with similar analgesia and methadone-type abuse profile.

notes: Schedule II in US; little contemporary use.

name: Morpheridine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Pethidine/meperidine 4-phenylpiperidine analogue with morpholinoethyl side chain. ~4× more potent than pethidine, μ-selective. Unlike pethidine, no convulsant liability.

notes: Schedule I under UN drug conventions; never marketed.

name: Glaucine

binding.notes: Halogenated derivatives studied (Asencio 2005); affinity 'poor and similar to' parent glaucine. Weak D1/D2 antagonism contributes to mild neuroleptic-like behavioural profile.
Glaucine is NOT a classical opioid — categorisation here is incorrect on a pharmacological basis. Its antitussive effect is non-opioid (Ca2+ block, PDE4 inhibition).

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Antitussive (Ca2+ channel + PDE4 inhibition); mild dopaminergic blockade; antinociception reported but mechanism unclear and only partly naloxone-reversible.

notes: Mis-classified as opioid in input — glaucine is an aporphine alkaloid antitussive (used in Bulgaria/EU) with no significant opioid receptor activity. Naloxone partially reverses some animal antinociception but the mechanism is not classical opioid agonism.

name: MGM-15

binding.notes: Matsumoto 2014 — μ/δ dual agonist; greater hMOR and hDOR affinity than 7-OH-mitragynine.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Dual μ/δ Gαi full agonist with high oral bioavailability — pharmacology of an addictive opioid despite the kratom-natural-product framing.

notes: Matsumoto/Horie 2014 dual μ/δ agonist derived from 7-OH-mitragynine. Has appeared in vendor markets recently as a 'kratom alternative' but exhibits the canonical pharmacology of an addictive full opioid agonist.

name: 2C-O-4

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: PIHKAL #25 (Shulgin). Threshold dose ~60 mg PO, weak +1 effects only. Shulgin abandoned the 2C-O series as 'uninteresting'. NOT an opioid — mis-categorised in input.

data_gaps_remaining: Ki at 5-HT2A; almost no quantitative pharmacology exists
notes: Phenethylamine psychedelic, NOT an opioid. Included in the classical-opioids batch by classification error in the input list.

name: Lean

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Mixture of codeine (~10 mg / 5 mL of typical formulation) + promethazine (~6.25 mg / 5 mL). Codeine pharmacology dominates the opioid effects; promethazine adds H1-antagonist sedation, D2 antagonism, anticholinergic effects, and cardiac Na+ channel/hERG block.

drug_interactions_pk.mechanism: pharmacodynamic — additive respiratory depression + QT prolongation (promethazine)

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: Codeine pharmacogenetics apply.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Promethazine QT prolongation contributes to lean's cardiac risk.

notes: Cultural shorthand for prescription codeine/promethazine cough syrup. Mortality risk reflects high single-event codeine doses (often 50-200 mg) combined with promethazine's QT and CNS-depressant effects, often plus alcohol.

class_name: Classical opioids and kratom-derived opioid alkaloids
shared_mechanism: Agonism (or antagonism) at the μ-opioid receptor (OPRM1), with variable activity at δ (OPRD1), κ (OPRK1), and NOP (OPRL1) receptors. Activated MOR couples Gαi/o → inhibits adenylyl cyclase (↓cAMP), activates GIRK potassium channels (hyperpolarisation), inhibits N/P/Q-type voltage-gated calcium channels (↓neurotransmitter release). Repeated activation drives GRK phosphorylation, β-arrestin-2 recruitment, desensitisation, and internalisation. 'Biased agonism' (G-protein > β-arrestin) was hypothesised to dissociate analgesia from respiratory depression (TRV130/oliceridine, kratom alkaloids) but the hypothesis is now contested (Conibear & Kelly 2019, doi:10.1016/j.tips.2019.04.002): much of the apparent safety of G-biased agonists like 7-OH-mitragynine and PZM21 derives from low intrinsic efficacy / partial agonism, not bias per se.
shared_pk_summary: Morphinans typically undergo UGT2B7 glucuronidation (morphine M3G/M6G, hydromorphone H3G, oxymorphone) — minimal CYP dependence. Codeine/hydrocodone/tramadol are CYP2D6 prodrugs — PMs get reduced effect, UMs get supratherapeutic active metabolite (codeine→morphine, hydrocodone→hydromorphone, tramadol→O-DSMT) and risk fatal respiratory depression at standard doses (FDA contraindicates codeine and tramadol <12 y, post-tonsillectomy adolescents). Oxycodone is primarily CYP3A4 (→inactive noroxycodone) with CYP2D6 minor (→oxymorphone). Methadone is mainly CYP2B6, with huge inter-individual half-life variability (8-59 h). Buprenorphine is CYP3A4 + UGT (very long t½, sublingual bioavailability ~30%). Mitragynine is CYP3A4-bioactivated to 7-OH-mitragynine in vivo.
shared_safety: Respiratory depression at supratherapeutic doses is the proximal cause of death. Naloxone reverses MOR-mediated opioid overdose; reversal of buprenorphine requires higher doses (slow off-rate), reversal of methadone may require multiple doses or infusion (long t½), reversal of meperidine does NOT prevent normeperidine seizures, and KOR-selective designer opioids (U-51754) are less responsive. Methadone uniquely carries hERG/QT risk (S-enantiomer ~3.5× more potent than R at hERG block). Dextropropoxyphene was withdrawn worldwide for cardiotoxicity (norpropoxyphene Na+/K+ channel block). Tramadol and tapentadol add SNRI/NRI activity → serotonin syndrome (tramadol > tapentadol) and lowered seizure threshold (tramadol particularly). Codeine/tramadol respiratory deaths in CYP2D6 UMs are the canonical pharmacogenetics safety case. OPRM1 A118G (rs1799971) G-carriers have ~30% higher morphine requirement and are paradoxically protected from morphine-induced respiratory depression.
sar_summary: Within the morphinan core: 3-OH free phenol (morphine) → CYP2D6 substrate; 3-O-methyl (codeine) → CYP2D6 prodrug (200× lower MOR affinity than morphine); 14-OH (oxycodone, oxymorphone, naloxone, naltrexone) → increased MOR affinity and altered receptor selectivity; 6-keto reduction (hydromorphone vs morphine) → 5-10× potency increase; 6-deoxy + 7,8-saturation (desomorphine) → 8-10× lipophilic potency increase; N-cyclopropylmethyl / N-allyl (naloxone, naltrexone, nalbuphine, buprenorphine, butorphanol) → switches efficacy toward antagonism or partial agonism; 6,14-endoetheno + thevinol/orvinol side chain (buprenorphine, etorphine, acetorphine) → sub-nanomolar MOR affinity, slow off-rate, and sometimes mixed efficacy (buprenorphine partial agonist; etorphine full agonist with 1000-3000× morphine potency). Outside morphinans: methadone/diphenylpropylamine class → MOR + NMDA + monoamine reuptake; piperidines (fentanyl, meperidine, ketobemidone) → variable; arylcyclohexylamines mostly NMDA (3-HO-PCP is the rare arylcyclohexylamine with high MOR affinity). Mitragynine indole alkaloids — biased G-protein signalling; bioactivated by CYP3A4 to 7-OH-mitragynine, the dominant in-vivo MOR effector; further N1-rearrangement gives mitragynine pseudoindoxyl (also biased).
